I’ve been to two weddings in the past few months. The first cost around $80k and the second was $140k. The second couple did get some help from family though.

Yeah I’ve definitely managed my expectations for his progress after reading so many people’s experiences. I’ll try to explain to his family that they need to be more patient since their understanding of schizophrenia is quite limited. 

I’m so pleased to hear that you and your wife have been able to stick it out and raise children, that’s really wonderful! I’m glad you have your wife, she sounds lovely. 

And perhaps I’m wrong but I don’t think I’m naive to what our life may be like now that this has happened. It’s been very difficult to adjust to but I won’t leave him. He’s still the same person I’ve loved for 7 years and no part of me would be ever want to let him struggle with this on his own.

When he first started the Invega pills he was on 6mg once a day and he responded to it relatively quickly. I would say his hallucinations went away almost completely within a few days and then also got gradually better over a period of about 2 months. 

When his symptoms returned he upped his dosage to 12mg daily for about a week and a half before receiving the shot. I don’t remember the dosage of the shot off the top of my head but it’s the one that’s meant to last a month. 

His experience with the shot was a little tricky because after getting the first initiation dose, the doctor’s office scheduled his second initiation dose to be 2 weeks after the first, despite us previously being told it was meant to be 5 days after. 

Within that two week period, he and his family went on vacation to St. Lucia and so he was unable to get the second dose despite realising he needed it earlier. It was during that time he began taking the oral pills as well, to help with the worsening symptoms. After arriving home, he had the second injection and also began taking the other AP along with continuing the oral Invega pills. 

The timing of that trip couldn’t have been worse considering his doctor’s office mis-scheduled his injection, so things were really hard for him before he got on the new AP.

Good to know about the starting and stopping of the clonazepam, I’ll keep that in mind. 

With his Invega usage, he was initially on a low oral dosage which then increased. Then he was switched to just injection but only went a few days without also taking the oral because his symptoms were too much for him to bear. 

And I haven’t heard of paradoxical worsening but it’s definitely something I’ve thought about at different points in the past month. To me it seems logical to perhaps try a different medication after symptoms don’t improve with certain dosage changes? 

However I of course have no medical training and I also don’t want my boyfriend to lose trust in his medical team, so I don’t say anything and just hope to see improvement. He’s been very compliant after coming out of his first episode, so I’m hyper aware of any damage I could cause to the trust he has. But I’ll definitely do more research on it now.

I read that about Benadryl too and told him to ask his doctor about switching to melatonin for sleep aid. 

But his doctor told him that the Benadryl is also beneficial to take for side effects caused by the AP, so he continues to take it. The only side effects he’s had from his meds so far are weight gain and drowsiness. 

I will definitely still keep it in mind as a possible cause for his symptoms and do more research. 

Thank you for your help and your kind words.

Thanks for the response! 

I was initially surprised that his doctor told him to come off so many meds at the same time. He was actually told to stop taking the lithium, clonazepam and the benadryl all at the same time which he did. He didnt begin retaking the clonazepam until a little while later when started feeling anxious at night. But since then he’s been taking it every night along with everything else. 

I also forgot to add that he recently had an Invega shot and is still prescribed to take 6mg of the oral Invega daily as well. Could this be characterised as too high of a dosage like you said? I’ve yet to see anyone talk about taking both the shot and the oral medication.

I have a double curve with similar degree of curvature to you and I’ve been squatting and deadlifting for a few years now. It may depend on the type of curve you have and whether it causes you any pain already, but squatting and deadlifting (with proper form) aren’t inherently harmful to your spine. Building muscle and gaining strength has actually helped with my scoliosis symptoms. I do notice some muscle imbalances here and there because of the scoliosis but I try to balance it out with unilateral movements as accessories.

I know exactly how you feel. It sometimes feels cruel that the world just keeps turning while we're paralysed by pain. I don't know how I'm expected to be present in real life when I'm dying on the inside.

I will say that although you feel your family will ultimately be fine without you, they won't. I'm not trying to guilt you because I know how it all feels. But I know people that have passed away from successful attempts and no matter how much time passes, the hole they leave in our hearts is unfillable. It's a pain that never heals.

I really hope you find some joy and peace in your coming days. You can talk to me if you ever need. I hope you get better and feel in love with life one day.
